### DescribeCloudAssistantStatus

Queries whether the Cloud Assistant client is installed on one or more Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances. If the Cloud Assistant client is installed, the system queries the total number of Cloud Assistant commands that have been run, the number of Cloud Assistant commands that are being run, and the time when Cloud Assistant commands were last run.

### SendFile

Sends a file to one or more Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances.

**Usage notes**

The instances to which you want to send a file must be in the Running ( `Running` ) state. The Cloud Assistant client must be installed on the instances. The file that you want to send must not exceed 32 KB in size after it is encoded in Base64. The file may fail to be sent due to instance exceptions, network exceptions, or exceptions on the Cloud Assistance client. Call the DescribeSendFileResults operation to troubleshoot the issues.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | SendFile | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to SendFile. |

| Content | String | Yes | #!/bin/bash echo "Current User is :" echo $(ps \| grep "$$" \| awk '{print $2}') ----- --- oss://bucketName/objectNa me | The content of the file. The content must not exceed 32 KB in size after it is encoded in Base64. If ContentType is set to PlainText , the value of Content is in plaintext. If ContentType is set to Base64 , the value of Content is Base64-encoded. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| InstanceId.N | RepeatList | Yes | i-bp185dy2o3o6n**** | The ID of instance N to which you want to send the file. Up to 50 instance IDs can be specified in each request. Valid values of N: 1 to 50. |
| Name | String | Yes | file.txt | The name of the file. The name supports all character sets and can be up to 255 characters in length. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao-**** | The region ID of the instance. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| TargetDir | String | Yes | /home | The destination directory on the instance to which you want to send the file. If the specified directory does not exist, the system creates the directory on the instance. |
| Description | String | No | This is a test file. | The description of the file. The description supports all character sets and can be up to 512 characters in length. |
| Timeout | Long | No | 60 | The timeout period for the file sending task. Unit: seconds. A timeout error occurs when a file cannot be sent because the process slows down or because a specific module or the Cloud Assistant client does not exist. If the specified timeout period is less than 10 seconds, the system sets the timeout period to 10 seconds to ensure that the file can be sent to the instances. Default value: 60. |
| ContentType | String | No | PlainText | The content type of the file. Valid values: PlainText Base64 Default value: PlainText. |
| FileOwner | String | No | root | The owner of the file. This parameter takes effect only for Linux instances. Default value: root. |
| FileGroup | String | No | root | The user group of the file. This parameter takes effect only for Linux instances. Default value: root. |
| FileMode | String | No | 0644 | The permissions on the file. This parameter takes effect only for Linux instances. You can configure this parameter in the same way as you configure the chmod command. Default value: 0644, which indicates that the owner of the file has the read and write permissions on the file and that the user group of the file and other users have the read- only permissions on the file. |
| Overwrite | Boolean | No | true | Specifies whether to overwrite a file in the destination directory if the file has the same name as the sent file. true false Default value: false. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| InvokeId | String | f-7d2a745b412b46**** | The ID of the file sending task. |
| RequestId | String | 473469C7-AA6F-4DC5-B3DB- A3DC0DE**** | The request ID. |

### DescribeSendFileResults

Queries the files sent by Cloud Assistant and their states.

**Usage notes**

When you send a file, the file may fail to be sent to specified Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances. You must call this operation to check the file sending results. You can call this operation to query the file sending records of the last two weeks. A maximum of 100,000 file sending records can be retained.

| PageSize | Long | No | 10 | The number of entries per page. Valid values: 1 to 50. Default value: 10. |

Valid values: Pending: The system is verifying or sending the file. If the sending state of the file on at least one instance is Pending, the overall sending state of the file is Pending. Running: The file creation task is running on the instances. If the sending state of the file on at least one instance is Running, the overall sending state of the file is Running. Success: If the sending state of the file on all the instances is Success, the overall sending state of the file is Success. Failed: If the sending state of the file on all the instances is Failed, the overall sending state of the file is Failed. If the sending state of the file on one or more instances is one of the following values, the overall sending state of the file is Failed: Invalid: The file is invalid. Aborted: The file failed to be sent. Failed: The file failed to be created. Timeout: The file sending task timed out. Error: An error occurred while the file was being sent. PartialFailed: The file was sent to some of the specified instances and failed to be sent to other instances. InstanceNotExists: The instance does not exist or was released. InstanceReleased: The instance was released while the file was being sent. InstanceNotRunning: The instance was not running when the file sending task was being created. AccountNotExists: The specified account does not exist. ClientNotRunning: The Cloud Assistant client was not running. ClientNotResponse: The Cloud Assistant client did not respond. ClientIsUpgrading: The Cloud Assistant client was being upgraded. ClientNeedUpgrade: The Cloud Assistant client needs to be upgraded. DeliveryTimeout: The file sending task timed out. FileCreateFail: The file failed to be created. FileAlreadyExists: A file with the same name already exists in the specified directory. FileContentInvalid: The file content is invalid. FileNameInvalid: The file name is invalid. FilePathInvalid: The specified directory is invalid. FileAuthorityInvalid: The specified permissions on the file are invalid. |

## Tags

### AddTags

You can call this operation to add or overwrite one or more tags on your ECS resources. You can add or overwrite tags on instances, disks, snapshots, images, and security groups to facilitate resource management. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: Up to 20 tags can be added to each ECS resource.

| Tag.N.Value | based on th |
|---|---|
| he same key ( | Tag.N.Key |

If you add a tag that has the same key ( `Tag.N.Key` ) as an existing tag on the specified resource, the new tag value ( `Tag.N.Value` ) overwrites the original tag value.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | AddTags | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to AddTags. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao-env17-d01 | The region ID of the resource on which you want to add or overwrite tags. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| ResourceType | String | Yes | instance | The type of the resource. Valid values: disk instance image securitygroup snapshot All values must be in lowercase. |
| ResourceId | String | Yes | i-bp1ecr********5go2go | The ID of the resource. When the value of the ResourceType parameter is instance, this parameter can be interpreted as InstanceId. |
| Tag.N.value | String | No | FinanceTagValue | The value of tag N to be bound to the resource. Note This parameter will be removed in the future. We recommend that you use the Tag.N.Value parameter to ensure future compatibility. |
| Tag.N.key | String | No | Finance | The key of tag N to be bound to the resource. Note This parameter will be removed in the future. We recommend that you use the Tag.N.Key parameter to ensure future compatibility. |
| Tag.N.Key | String | No | Finance | The key of tag N to be bound to the resource. Valid values of N: 1 to 20. The tag key cannot be an empty string. It can be up to 128 characters in length and cannot contain http:// or https://. It cannot start with acs: or aliyun. |
| Tag.N.Value | String | No | FinanceTagValue | The value of tag N to be bound to the resource. Valid values of N: 1 to 20. The tag value can be an empty string. It can be up to 128 characters in length and cannot contain http:// or https://. It cannot start with acs: or aliyun. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | 473469C7-AA6F-4DC5-B3DB- A3DC0DE3C83E | The ID of the request. |

https://ecs.example.com/?Action=AddTags &RegionId=cn-qingdao-env17-d01 &ResourceType=instance &ResourceId=i-bp1ecr5g**** &Tag.1.Key=Finance &Tag.1.Value=FinanceTagValue &<Common request parameters>

### DescribeTags

You can call this operation to query available tags. You can query tags by specifying filter conditions such as resource type, resource ID, tag key, and tag value. The specified filter conditions have logical AND relations. Only the tags that meet all the specified filter conditions are returned. If a tag key is specified and no tag values are specified, all tags that contain the tag key are returned. If a tag key-value pair is specified, only tags that exactly match the key-value pair are returned.

| Tag.N.Key | String | No | Finance | The key of tag N bound to the resource. Valid values of N: 1 to 20. The tag key cannot be an empty string. It can be up to 64 characters in length and cannot contain http:// or https://. It cannot start with acs: or aliyun. |

| Tag.N.Value | String | No | Finance | The value of tag N bound to the resource. Valid values of N: 1 to 20. The tag value can be an empty string. It can be up to 128 characters in length and cannot contain http:// or https://. It cannot start with acs: or aliyun. |

In the specified tags, a single tag key may correspond to one or more tag values. Fuzzy search may have a latency of 2 seconds. A fuzzy search can return a result set of up to 5,000 resources. When you use TagFilter.N.TagKey for fuzzy search of ECS resources, you must leave TagFilter.N.TagValues.N empty. For example, to query ECS resources that have the tag with the environment tag key added, you can set TagFilter.1.TagKey to env , but you must leave TagFilter.1.TagValues empty. When you use TagFilter.N.TagValues.N for fuzzy search of ECS resources, you must set TagFilter.N.TagKey to an exact value. ## Appendix

### Terms

This topic describes the terms that may be used in ECS API operations.

**Terms**

The following table describes the terms that may be used in ECS API operations.

| Term | Full name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| instance | Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance | An ECS instance is a virtual computer that uses the computing resources available in a physical machine. |
| region |   | A region is a separate geographic area where resources reside. Each region consists of one or more zones. |
| zone | zone | A physical area with an independent network and power supply. A region can be divided into multiple zones. Network latency is short for communication between ECS instances in the same zone. Zones in each region are connected over the internal network. When a zone becomes unavailable, the other zones are not affected. |
| image | image file | An image file can be built based on the data of an operating system and applications. You can select an image to initialize an ECS instance. An image contains all data necessary to create an ECS instance. The system disk of a new instance is a complete copy of the image that is used to create the instance, and contains the operating system and software configurations from the image. To create instances of different operating systems, you must select different image files. |
| disk |   | A disk is a storage device used by an instance. |
| snapshot |   | A snapshot is a copy of data on a disk for a specific point in time. A snapshot can be used to restore disk data and create custom images. |
| IP | IP address | A public IP address. |
| security group | security group | A security group acts as a virtual firewall to control traffic to or from ECS instances. Each ECS instance must belong to at least one security group. You can create security group rules in security groups. The security group rules of a security group apply to all instances in the security group. |
| CIDR | Classless Inter-Domain Routing | CIDR is a new addressing scheme for the Internet and allows for more efficient allocation of IP addresses than the old Class A, B, and C addressing schemes. For example, to convert the IP address segment 10.203.96.0 to 10.203.127.255 into a CIDR block, find the same first 19 bits. 10.203.0110 0000.0000 0000 to 10.203.0111 1111.1111 1111 can be represented by 10.203.96.0/19. |

**Limits**

ECS enforces quotas on the number of instances, security groups, and other resources that can be used by each user. Limits apply to instance types, the number of disks per instance, disk capacity, and the number of disk snapshots.

### How to ensure idempotency

If a request timeout or internal server error occurs when you call CreateInstance to create an ECS instance, the client may attempt to resend the request. You can specify the **ClientToken** parameter to prevent the server from creating redundant instances in these cases. The
**ClientToken** parameter ensures idempotency of the request.
A **ClientToken** is a unique and case-sensitive string generated by the client. It cannot exceed 64 ASCII characters in length. If you use the same **ClientToken** for multiple CreateInstance operations, the server will return identical responses that contain the same
**InstanceId** parameter. Therefore, if an error occurs during an instance creation request, you can retry the creation request using the same
**ClientToken** as the failed request. This ensures that only one ECS instance is created and that it assigned to a specific **InstanceId**.
If you specify a **ClientToken** that is in use with different request parameters than previously used, ECS will return the
**IdempotentParameterMismatch** error code. You must change the **SignatureNonce**, **Timestamp**, and **Signature** values when calling the
operation again. This is because ECS uses **SignatureNonce** to prevent replay attacks and **Timestamp** to mark the time of each request. Each new request must have different **SignatureNonce** and **Timestamp** values, which changes the **Signature** value. Typically, if a 500 (InternalError) or 503 (ServiceUnavailable) error code is returned or no responses are returned, you must retry operations. If an operation is retried after a response code of 200 is returned, an identical response will be returned but the server status will not be affected. If a 4xx error code is returned and try it later does not appear in the error message, attempts to retry the operation will fail.

### API behavior when an instance is locked for

**security reasons**

When OperationLocks in the DescribeInstances response contains LockReason: security for an instance, the instance is locked for security reasons. If a disk on the instance is in the In_use state, the behavior of API operations related to the disk is subject to the OperationLocks settings of the instance. If the disk is in other states, the OperationLocks settings can be ignored. Table 1. Operations and behavior

|---|---|
| AttachDisk | Returns an error. |
| AuthorizeSecurityGroup | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| CreateDisk | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| CreateImage | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| CreateInstance | - |
| CreateSecurityGroup | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| CreateSnapshot | Returns an error when the disk is attached to the current instance and is in theI nuse state. _ |

| DeleteImage | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |

| DeleteInstance | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |

| ModifyAutoSnapshotPolicy | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| ModifyDiskAttribute | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| ModifyInstanceAttribute | Returns an error. |
| RebootInstance | Returns an error. |
| ReInitDisk | Returns an error when the disk is attached to the current instance and is in the Inuse state When the _ disk is attached to the current instance and is in other states, the operation is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| ReplaceSystemDisk | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| ResetDisk | Returns an error. |
| RevokeSecurityGroup | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| StartInstance | Returns an error. |
| StopInstance | Returns an error. |

### ISO 8601 date and time formats

ISO 8601 Data elements and interchange formats – Information interchange – Representation of dates and times is an international standard covering the exchange of date- and time-related data. It was issued by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). ECS open APIs adopt the ISO 8601 standard date and time formats.
